items.title: Morning Briefing: Nov. 12
items.excerpt: Here’s a rundown of all the news you need to start your Thursday, including US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arriving in Moscow for talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin, Israeli security cabinet ordering military to preparing for possible attack on Iran, and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan highlighting importance of cleaner and more sustainable world for future generations during COP31. ... - Israeli security cabinet orders military to prepare for possible attack on Iran: Report Israel’s security cabinet has instructed the military to step up preparations for a possible attack on Iran, Israeli public broadcaster KAN reported Wednesday evening. “The directives issued by the security cabinet to the Israeli military could lead it to carry out activities that could trigger a war,” the broadcaster said. KAN said the directives were made public after Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot issued a statement urging caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to refrain from unnecessary military operations until the next government is formed. The security cabinet last met on Oct. 5 – weeks before the Oct. 27 Israeli elections – the broadcaster added. - Turkish president urges cleaner, greener, fairer ... Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan highlighted on Wednesday the importance of leaving a cleaner and more sustainable world for future generations during COP31, the UN Climate Change Conference in Türkiye. ... - An Israeli airstrike killed four Palestinians at Nasser Medical Complex in southern Gaza early Thursday, said Civil Defense spokesman Mahmoud Basal. ... - Russia and Ukraine have agreed "in principle" on a new large-scale prisoner exchange, with details to be announced soon, the head of the Russian delegation at talks in Abu Dhabi said. - Scott Colom wins Mississippi Senate race, giving state its 1st Democratic senator in nearly 4 decades. - Pope Leo XIV arrived in Peru on Wednesday for a historic six-day pastoral visit, meeting President Keiko Fujimori at the Government Palace in Lima shortly after landing in his adopted homeland. ... - Iran's deputy chief of the General Staff of the Armed Forces warned that US military bases and interests were within range of Iranian missiles and drones, saying Tehran was prepared to strike targets beyond the region in the event of renewed attacks. - The number of confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo has crossed 11,000 since the outbreak was declared in May, official data showed as health authorities struggle to contain the largest outbreak in the country. ... - Police confronted striking workers and protesters blocked roads in Spain as the country held its first general strike in 14 years, demanding affordable housing and higher wages ahead of a national election.

items.title: AP News Summary at 3:48 a.m. EST | National | guardonline.com
items.excerpt: US envoys go to meet Putin at the Kremlin following Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi MOSCOW (AP) — Envoys for U.S. President Donald Trump have arrived in Moscow to discuss U.S.-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine. Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff attended negotiations in Abu Dhabi which ended Wednesday with an agreement on a prisoner exchange. But no significant progress was made on ending the nearly five-year conflict. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy welcomed the prisoner exchange but insisted Ukraine won't cede territory for peace. Russia and Ukraine remain divided on key issues including post-conflict security and European involvement in talks. Kushner aims to include European countries in future discussions. HONG KONG (AP) — Megaspeed, the Singapore-headquartered data center company linked to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s scandal, has pledged to cooperate with a U.S. investigation into potential risks to national security. Nvidia’s board of directors was reported to be meeting to discuss Huang’s situation, but there was no immediate word on any outcome from those discussions. In its first statement since Huang admitted to having an affair with a former Megaspeed executive, the company said that it takes its obligation to comply with U.S. export control laws “extremely seriously.” It said in a statement that it was committed "to working constructively and transparently with the U.S. government.” JACKSON, Miss. (AP) — Mississippi has elected its first Black U.S. senator since post-Civil War Reconstruction and delivered Democrats a major upset in a rocky midterm election for the GOP. Scott Colom defeated Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in the Deep South state that has been controlled mostly by white conservatives for generations. Colom noted Mississippi's civil rights history in his Wednesday night victory speech but pledged to represent all Mississippians. The Associated Press called the contest Wednesday evening. Hyde-Smith posted a concession video on social media. National and Mississippi Democrats are celebrating the win as a seismic shift in the state and region. Colom capitalized on the state’s large Black population, discontent with the economy and Hyde-Smith’s mistakes. ... KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Ukrainians are preparing for a challenging winter as the war continues. Many expect it to be the hardest yet, with the energy system struggling under constant attacks. Since August, Kyiv has faced daily air raid threats and strikes on critical infrastructure. Some residents, like Kateryna Tsvihun, have decided to leave the city to protect their children. Others, unable to afford relocation, are staying and preparing for potential power and heating outages. Officials warn that Russia aims to create a crisis in Kyiv, impacting the morale of the entire country. Residents are relying on air defense, utility workers, and community support. KHAN YOUNIS, Gaza Strip (AP) — Gaza’s Health Ministry says an Israeli airstrike has hit one of the main hospitals still operating in the Gaza Strip, killing six people, including a surgeon and a 13-year-old boy. The Israeli military said the strike Thursday on Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza was targeting a Hamas commander and other militants, without providing evidence. The commander it identified was not among the dead. The ministry and witnesses said the strike hit the hospital’s surgical wing. Footage showed several wards and operating rooms heavily damaged or destroyed, with debris scattered across hospital beds and equipment and rebar dangling from holes in the ceiling. At least 28 people were wounded. NEW YORK (AP) — New York City’s mayor says at least eight people have died after a three-story building in Brooklyn collapsed at the edge of a construction site. The announcement Thursday from Mayor Zohran Mamdani came as firefighters kept digging through the rubble to find others who may be trapped beneath the wreckage. The structure fell at the edge of a construction site on Wednesday afternoon. Rescuers worked overnight into Thursday, using dogs to sniff for survivors. The cause of the collapse is under investigation. The three-story building was a mixed-use structure with apartments above commercial space. Mamdani says at least 17 people have been injured, including three firefighters. WASHINGTON (AP) — Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is under scrutiny after revelations of an affair with Chinese businessperson Alice Huang, who's suspected of spying. Nvidia produces crucial AI chips that both China and the U.S. covet, and Jensen Huang's affair has sparked concerns about national security. The Department of Justice is investigating whether a company tied to Alice Huang illegally funneled chips to China. Nvidia's board says there's “no reason to believe” secrets were compromised. President Donald Trump is a supporter of Jensen Huang and has played down the issue. China has denied the allegations that Alice Huang was a spy. LIMA, Peru (AP) — Pope Leo XIV has declared Peru his “homeland” as he arrived in Lima Wednesday at the start of his historic visit. Leo credits Peruvians with having formed him as a pastor by sharing their lives, joys and struggles with him. A nationwide party erupted to welcome the country's beloved “Padre Robert” home. The visit to Peru marks the final leg of Leo’s three-nation South America tour. Peru is seen as the emotional highlight of his trip because of the more than two decades that the former Robert Prevost spent in Peru as a missionary priest and later bishop. He is a dual citizen of the United States and Peru.

items.title: Treasury yields rise as investors await inflation and housing data
items.excerpt: Published Thu, Nov 12 2026 2:38 AM EST Hugh Leask U.S. Treasury yields edged higher Thursday as bond trading resumed after the Veterans Day closure and investors looked ahead to fresh inflation and housing data for clues about the economy and the Federal Reserve's next move. The yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury Add To Watchlist note — the benchmark for mortgages, auto loans and credit card debt — was up 2 basis points at 5.0100%. The 2-year Treasury note Add To Watchlist yield, which is more sensitive to short-term Federal Reserve interest rate decisions, was 5 basis points higher at 4.7800%. The longer-dated 30-year Treasury note Add To Watchlist yield — which often moves on geopolitical developments — was steady at 5.3503%. One basis point equals 0.01%, or 1/100th of 1%, and yields and prices move inversely to one another. The rise in yields comes as traders await more domestic data releases this week for fresh insights into the U.S. economic picture. On Friday, the latest monthly producer price inflation print, which tracks wholesale inflation, is expected to show a 0.4% rise in October, down from the 1.3% surge in September. Before that, investors are also looking out for October's home sales report from the National Association of Realtors, due later Thursday. Existing home sales rose by 1.5% in September to 3.99 million, up from a two-year low the previous month, and are expected to reach 4 million last month, according to Trading Economics estimates.

items.title: Up First briefing: Scott Colom; Trump; Russia-Ukraine talks; El-Sayed : NPR
items.excerpt: November 12, 2026 7:15 AM ET ... Democrat Scott Colom has won the U.S. Senate seat from Mississippi, defeating Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith by just a few thousand votes. Colom will be the first Black Senator from the state in nearly 150 years. His win expands the Democratic majority in the new Congress to 55 seats. The Alaska race is still undecided. ... - 🎧 Colom's win highlights growing voter concerns about affordability and the impact of the war in Iran, Elise Catrion Gregg of the Gulf States Newsroom and Mississippi Public Broadcasting tells Up First. During her campaign, Hyde-Smith relied on her record and President Trump's support, which Gregg says is no longer a winning strategy. This race signals a potential national shift, showing that the South is becoming a viable target for Democrats, Gregg says. - ➡️ A U.S. Supreme Court ruling this year weakened the Voting Rights Act, raising the possibility of a record drop in Black Congressional representation. The Democratic blue wave lessened the expected decline, but an NPR analysis shows that Black representation in the U.S. House is still slated to decrease with the incoming Congress. The White House is warning Democrats that their planned investigations into administration officials could cross the line into "blatant criminality." White House Counsel Will Scharf said in a letter to Rep. Robert Garcia, who is expected to lead the House Oversight Committee next year, that the administration is monitoring "abusive and capricious threats" from Democrats. The letter concludes by saying that "the administration will not be extorted and will not be cowed by unlawful process, motivated by animus, pettiness, hatred or any other unlawful motive to intimidate, penalize or interfere with the lawful functioning of government." Garcia said Democrats will not be deterred by threats from the Department of Justice or Trump's lawyers. - 🎧 The administration's arguments may buy time and push Democrats to go to court to enforce their subpoenas, NPR's Tamara Keith says. She adds that the White House letter gives a preview of the legal arguments the administration might use next year. But more importantly, Keith says that it signals that the White House and Justice Department won't accept congressional investigations and oversight without a fight. Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a significant prisoner swap after two days of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi. Trump's envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff are now in Moscow today to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin and attempt to make more headway to end the war in Ukraine. - 🎧 NPR's Charles Maynes says that, going into the talks in Abu Dhabi, U.S. officials were exploring Article 5-like guarantees for Ukraine, similar to NATO's collective security defense. A move like this would be significant if implemented, but Moscow has already rejected the concept of a "NATO lite" status for Ukraine and its full NATO membership. Kushner said that, in Moscow, he aims to brief Putin directly and persuade him to involve Europeans in discussions about European security. European leaders, concerned about potential deals made without their input, are expected to join Kushner and Witkoff after these talks, when they'll meet with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Ireland.

items.title: Colorado Democrats heading to Congress seek ...
items.excerpt: With a fresh crop of Democrats set to be sworn in to a Congress their party will control next year, many of Colorado’s newly elected and incumbent representatives intend to prioritize accountability for the executive branch. Democrats from Colorado have generally supported measures that have sought to call out allegedly corrupt and unlawful conduct by President Donald Trump and his members of his administration since he returned to office in 2025. With incoming Democratic majorities in both chambers, the chances of those efforts being successful will be much more likely. Three of Colorado’s four current Democrats in the House voted to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday. The fourth Democrat, U.S. Rep.
